---
title: "About"
---

I am a biopharmaceutical scientist and Lecturer in the Basic Sciences Department at the Michael Chilufya Sata School of Medicine (MCSSoM), Copperbelt University (CBU), Ndola, Zambia. I completed a Doctor of Pharmaceutical Sciences at Hokkaido University, Japan, in 2019 and joined CBU in September 2019. I have since served as Head of the Basic Sciences Department and, in December 2022, as Acting Dean, and I have coordinated undergraduate research at the School since 2015.

## Teaching

I set and moderate immunology assessments for BSc Biomedical Sciences students, including the fourth-year MBM 425 Immunology examination and the fifth-year assessments linked to hospital placements.

## Research interests

My work spans pharmacogenomics, structural biology (AlphaFold2, GROMACS, CASTp and FoldX), bioinformatics, implementation science for non-communicable diseases, biostatistics, and research ethics governance. A recurring thread is the question of who produces health evidence in Zambia, and where.

## Roles

- Programme Development Lead, proposed MSc and DSc in Pharmacogenomics and Personalised Medicine
- Work Package 5 (Core Modules) Lead, IS4NCDs
- Country Representative for Zambia, African Bioethics Network
- Establishing the Centre for Computational Health Sciences at CBU
- Incoming HIGH IRI Fellow, Washington University in St. Louis (in residence, Cape Town)
